meta.title: 3D Bioprinting Pluripotent Stem Cell Derived Neural Tissues Using a Novel Fibrin Bioink Containing Drug Releasing Microspheres.

extracted_by: seed: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: hiPSC-derived neural progenitors were printed in a fibrin bioink containing guggulsterone-releasing microspheres on the RX1 printer. Tissues were over 90% viable and expressed dopaminergic and glial markers after 30 days.

formulations.crosslinking: CaCl2 + chitosan + thrombin crosslinker, co-extruded in microfluidic printhead
formulations.review_notes: Pressure converted from 50 mbar (bioink channel). Marker percentages are reported for the construct overall.
formulations.name: Fibrin bioink + guggulsterone-loaded microspheres (GM)
formulations.composition_detail: 20 mg/mL fibrinogen, 0.5% w/v alginate, 0.3 mg/mL genipin
formulations.key_outcome: Guggulsterone microspheres gave the highest day-7 viability (98%) and supported TH+ dopaminergic neurons at day 30.

evidence.quote: NPCs at a concentration of 1 million cells/mL were thawed and resuspended in the bioink composed of 20 mg/mL of fibrinogen
The printing speed used was 25 mm/s and pressure for bioink, crosslinker and buffer channels were 50 mbar, 60 mbar, and 100 mbar, respectively.
Constructs from all groups showed high viability 1-day post-printing: GM (92 ± 3%), UM (78 ± 11%), SG (89 ± 2%)
The GM group exhibited the highest level of viability on day 7 (98 ± 1%)
